headline: Red Sox bats take a nap in maddening one-run loss
morning_brew: I watched that game against the Athletics through my fingers like I was witnessing a horror movie, except the only thing dying on screen was my mood. After the offensive fireworks we saw earlier in the week, seeing the bats go dead silent until the final two innings was a total disastah. Jake Bennett actually pitched well enough to win, giving us six and a third innings of three-run ball, but you cannot expect to win when you don't start scoring until the eighth. It is the kind of loss that makes you want to drive a rusty screw through your remote, especially knowing we had chances to break it open early.

The bullpen ended up being the difference, and not in a good way. Ryan Watson gave up that run in the eighth, and suddenly a game that felt winnable turned into a sour result. I have not seen a lineup look that confused since cousin Jimmy tried to hit a beach ball with a broom in his backyard, missing every single swing like his life depended on it. We needed someone to step up, and instead, we handed the Athletics a win they did not really have to work all that hard for. It is frustrating because this team has shown they can hang with anyone, but consistency remains our biggest enemy.

We are sitting at 55-51, and we have to put this one behind us fast. The road trip continues tonight, and we need to bounce back before things get any tighter in the standings. There is no time to sulk about one bad night when you are fighting for a wild card spot, but man, this one really burns. Let us see if the guys can come out with a little more fire in their bellies tonight. The Duck Boat fund is feeling a little light after last night, and I am not looking to make any more withdrawals.

news_digest.headline: Brian Serven hits 1st MLB homer since 2022 and Jump pitches A's to 4-3 win over Red Sox
news_digest.dans_take: Giving up a first career home run to a guy who had not hit one in years is just the kind of vintage Boston sports misery I expect.
